DT Guardian

A simulated, offline-first edge controller for a 200 kVA distribution transformer. An IS 2026-7 thermal model drives MILP dispatch of battery storage, EV charging and pump loads, with a fail-safe fallback when the forecast or solver fails.

$ cat problem.md

Schneider Electric Yuva Yodha Energy Tech Hackathon, Challenge 3 (grid reliability and renewable intermittency), prototype round. The project aims to turn a distribution transformer's thermal headroom into neighbourhood flexibility: EV and pump demand shifts toward renewable-rich hours, and critical loads stay on during supply gaps.

The prototype is a Python simulator with a thermal twin, a load forecaster, a rolling-horizon dispatcher, baselines and an experiment pipeline. It is an offline-first edge controller.

$ cat limits.md

  • No field deployment and no utility integration. This is a prototype-round entry.
  • The electrical model uses a voltage proxy. OpenDSS integration and the dashboard are unfinished.
  • The outage result covers a simulated 6-hour, battery-stressed outage only.

Code is private until the competition ends.
